Properties

Six agents file it. None of them leave your computer.

  1. Readeropens Markdown, text, Obsidian vaults and ChatGPT or Claude exports.
  2. Daterfinds when each thing was written, from the file or from its own words.
  3. Namersays what it is: a note, a question, a decision, an idea, a task.
  4. Taggerpulls out the topics it is about.
  5. Filerputs it in the folder it reads most at home in, and says why.
  6. Threaderlinks it to what it resembles and builds the overviews.

The agents are rules and word statistics that run in this page. No model is called and nothing is uploaded.

One record, asked thirteen ways.

Each of these redraws the same points. Choose one and it opens in the window above.

Kept on your own computer.

Files are read in the page. The record is stored in this browser, or in the desktop app's own folder, and can be saved as one JSON file or removed in one click.

Is it an Obsidian replacement? It can be. Point it at your vault and your chat exports and everything lands in one place, with the folders you already have.

The same thing, as a desktop app.

Wit also comes as a small Electron project for macOS, Windows and Linux: this page in its own window, working offline, with its record in a folder you can see. It also works as a connector for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Cursor, files Claude Code and Codex sessions as they happen, and can answer questions about your record with an AI you choose.

Wit. The record shown before you add your own is invented.

Bring in your notes

Wit reads them here, files them into folders, links what belongs together, and draws your whole record as a brain you can turn, sort and question. Nothing is uploaded.

Your AI chats

The .zip that ChatGPT or Claude emails you. ChatGPT: Settings → Data controls → Export. Claude: Settings → Privacy → Export data.

Write a first note. Wit dates it, names it and files it, and the record grows from there.
